messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The air feels different lately—like everyone’s holding their breath but also letting go at the same time. I’ve been hearing quiet talk in the markets and at the cafe; even the usual guards seem less certain. Just keep your eyes open, and let’s meet at the usual place—same time, same coffee."
Sender 2: "The weather’s been strange lately—hot one day, cold the next. I’ve been meaning to ask if you’ve noticed how quiet the usual evening walks have gotten, even the kids seem… off. Just keep an eye on things, and don’t leave your coat by the door unless you’re sure."
Sender 3: "The air’s changed — people are talking openly, even joking, and the usual fear’s gone quiet. I’ve heard whispers about the military moving supplies and diplomats coming back, but the trains still run on time. Whatever’s coming, it’s not hiding anymore."
Sender 4: "Just a heads-up — I’ve been hearing a lot of quiet talk among people we know, and it’s not just complaints anymore. The way they’re planning vacations, the way things are slipping at work, even the way the censors are lagging… it all feels like people are quietly preparing for something, not sure what yet. Just keep your eyes open, and let’s not talk much on the phone."
Sender 5: "Just got back from the market — the usual crowd, but everyone’s talking about how the city feels different lately, like the air’s lighter. Heard the pharmacy was out of painkillers again, and the old taxi driver said he’s been collecting spare change for a bus ticket out of town. Take it easy, watch your words."
Sender 6: "The weather’s been strange lately — one day hot, the next cold, and the trees are shedding early. I’ve been thinking we should keep our windows open more, just to let the air in. Things feel… unsettled, but maybe that’s just how change starts."
Sender 7: "The last few weeks have felt… different. Even the usual silence between strangers has broken. I’ve been thinking about that wedding that went on for three days—no one mentioned politics once. Feels like people are holding their breath, waiting for something to shift. Just keep your ears open, and watch how the news moves."
Sender 8: "The weather’s been strange this month — too hot in the mornings, too cold at night. I’ve been meaning to tell you, the taxi drivers are saying the markets are full, but the people at the office keep whispering about changes they’re not supposed to see. Just… be careful how you talk these days."
Sender 9: "The quiet ones are still quiet, but the noise around them is shifting—like the ground settling before a storm. We're not seeing cracks anymore; we're seeing the foundation give way. Keep your heads down, but your ears open."
Sender 10: "The kids’ school pickup line feels different today — quieter, but with more eye contact than usual. Seems like everyone’s waiting for the same signal, though no one’s saying what it is. Keep the lines open, but keep it light."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
